title: Ukban the Babylonian
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman summarizes Sanhedrin 31b as follows. They sent word from the Land of Israel to Mar Ukva to make peace between Ukban and his brother Yirmiyah. If he would not listen to him, he was to persuade him to go to Tiberias. See there.

notes.text: The consulted letter names Ukban the Babylonian as the complainant and Yirmiyah as his brother. Hyman’s compressed pronouns leave the precise mediation and refusal roles unclear; Mar Ukva is not identified with Ukban.

The saved whole Davidson Sanhedrin31b letter names Mar Ukva as recipient and Ukban the Babylonian as complainant against his brother Yirmiyah. Naming Ukban in the body clarifies that first pronoun without identifying him with Mar Ukva. Hyman’s make-peace and refusal-condition wording remains his summary. The later him referents are left open; no newly inspected Rashi determines them. Supplied ישיאו is singular he should persuade him, rather than the earlier plural proposal.

The letter addresses Mar Ukva and names Ukban the Babylonian as the complainant against his brother Yirmiyah. Rashi explains that they were to urge Yirmiyah to reconcile and require him to come to Tiberias for a hearing. Rashi gives two readings of the grievance in the letter. The explicit refusal condition is part of Hyman’s paraphrase.
